account: At about 2 a.m. on 6 August 2025, a woman in her 70s identified as “A” was at home in Deogam-dong, Daedeok-gu, Daejeon, South Korea. She lives alone and has schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. She repeatedly told the city-issued AI care robot Kkumdori “I want to die” and “save me”. The robot's crisis-detection algorithm flagged the words and alerted the operator's control center. A staff member phoned her. When she kept repeating them, staff reported to police on 112 with her location. Officers found her emotionally unstable and contacted her family. Police judged hospital treatment urgent. On the afternoon of 7 August she was admitted with her guardian's consent. Daejeon announced the case on 13 August 2025.

ai_role.statement: The robot's crisis-detection algorithm recognized repeated danger words (“죽고 싶다”, “살려줘”) in conversation at 2 a.m. It sent an alert to a human control center. People did everything after that: the check-in call, the 112 report with location, the police visit, the family contact and the admission. The city's welfare director says the alert is what made the rapid dispatch and protection possible. Whether A would have come to harm that night is not established. Every account derives from the city's 13 August briefing.

data.retained_case_account: At about 2 a.m. on 6 August 2025, a woman in her 70s identified as “A” was at home in Deogam-dong, Daedeok-gu, Daejeon, South Korea. She lives alone and has schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. She repeatedly told the city-issued AI care robot Kkumdori “I want to die” and “save me”. The robot's crisis-detection algorithm flagged the words and alerted the operator's control center. A staff member phoned her. When she kept repeating them, staff reported to police on 112 with her location. Officers found her emotionally unstable and contacted her family. Police judged hospital treatment urgent. On the afternoon of 7 August she was admitted with her guardian's consent. Daejeon announced the case on 13 August 2025.

They offer companionship, medication and schedule reminders and health monitoring. They detect crisis signs such as suicide risk and depression and automatically notify agencies and guardians. The alert was that function.

ratings.reason: A woman in her 70s living alone, with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, was in acute crisis at 2 a.m. She got a check-in call, a police visit that night and protective hospital admission the next afternoon. The city and the headlines call it life-saving. But no attempt was reported, so the counterfactual is unproven. Her guardian said the robot being beside her was a great support.

Daejeon's welfare office gained a demonstrated case for its 1,000-robot program. Its director cited it as a model. A 2026 Yonhap report says the city will continue the policy on the strength of such cases.
